query: select * from tasks where title like '%chronic%' or local_id like '%dettid-alignment%' or local_id in (select task_id from task_notes where content like '%/pull/3096%')

rows.title: Clear check.portability_paths, the cheapest of three chronic main reds
rows.description:
- **MEASURED IN RUN 1866 AT PR 3090's HEAD 80ce2ee94689: 269 of 270 nodes executed, 3 failed, 1 skipped, 34m17s at -j 16. The three failures — check.portability_paths, e2e.manifest_c_programs, e2e.manifest_backend_parity_c — ARE CHRONIC MAIN REDS AND NONE IS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THAT PULL REQUEST, which was checked rather than assumed.**
- **THE OWNING LANE NAMES THIS ONE AS BY FAR THE CHEAPEST: it is ONE LEGACY FIXTURE FILE. Start here rather than with the two e2e nodes.**
- **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE NODE: these same three block the pin bump, hermit 3066, and at least one other landing. They are the shared dependency, so clearing them unblocks several things rather than one.**
- ⚠️ **ESTABLISH THAT THE FAILURE IS THE FIXTURE BEFORE CHANGING THE FIXTURE. A node named portability_paths failing on a legacy file is exactly the shape where the file is a symptom and a path assumption elsewhere is the cause — this project has repeatedly found a cell name pointing at the wrong subsystem, most recently a hardware-trap cell whose cause was host-timed polling.**
- ⚠️ **DO NOT CLEAR IT BY RELAXING THE CHECK OR RETIRING THE FIXTURE. A node that goes green because it stopped looking is worse than one that is red, and these three have survived long enough that the convenient fix will be tempting. If the honest answer is that the fixture encodes an obsolete expectation, say so explicitly with evidence rather than deleting it quietly.**
- **CONTEXT WORTH HAVING: the trajectory is strongly positive and the earlier figures make that checkable — 14 executed with zero tests before PR 3080, then 79 executed with 191 skipped, now 269 of 270. check.lint_checks and test.regular_crates cleared on their own.**
- **Verify:** the node passes at current main, the failure is shown to have been real rather than a stale expectation, and no assertion, tolerance or case was weakened to achieve it.

rows.title: Clear the two chronic e2e manifest reds blocking the pin and three landings
rows.description:
- **e2e.manifest_c_programs (206 retained logs) and e2e.manifest_backend_parity_c (77) ARE THE LAST TWO OF THE FIVE CHRONIC MAIN REDS. check.lint_checks and test.regular_crates cleared on their own; check.portability_paths was cleared with all 8 legacy fixture files re-hashed byte-identical and nothing weakened, retired or deleted.**
- **THEY BLOCK MORE THAN ONE THING: the reverie pin bump, hermit 3066, and at least one further landing all wait on this same pair. That is why they are worth attacking directly rather than routing around.**
- **THE MEASURED CONTEXT, so the scale is checkable: RUN 1866 at 80ce2ee94689 executed 269 of 270 nodes in 34m17s at -j 16 with 3 failures. Before PR 3080 the same profile managed 14 executed, 1 failed, 256 skipped and ZERO tests.**
- ⚠️ **DO NOT CLEAR THESE BY RELAXING AN ASSERTION, RETIRING A CELL OR WIDENING A TOLERANCE. They have survived long enough that the convenient fix will look reasonable, and a node that passes because it stopped looking is worse than one that is red. If a cell encodes an obsolete expectation, say so with evidence rather than deleting it.**
- ⚠️ **206 AND 77 RETAINED LOGS ARE AN ASSET RATHER THAN A BURDEN — that is a large evidence base for establishing whether these are one cause or two. Establish that before fixing either; this project has repeatedly found cells grouped by name that had different causes, and cells with different names that shared one.**
- **ENVIRONMENT HAZARD HIT THREE TIMES TONIGHT BY THE SAME LANE: a fresh worktree has no submodules, so a rust-script test invocation there fails for a reason unrelated to the code under test.**
- **Verify:** both nodes pass at current main in a full-profile run, with the cause named for each and an explicit statement that no assertion, tolerance, cell or case was weakened.

rows.title: Restore the DetTid alignment without spawning a host thread
rows.description:
- **FILED BEFORE THE REVERT THAT CREATES IT, SO THE OBLIGATION EXISTS RATHER THAN BEING PROMISED. Three lines in hermit-cli/src/bin/hermit/tracing.rs from https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2945, commit 1d9c9094dea0e7a4a85bb641165088bded1386bd, are being reverted as the immediate unblock for c-programs/setitimer-determinism under kvm.**
- **WHAT THE REVERT GIVES BACK: the identity mismatch 2945 set out to fix. equalize_tracing_thread_number aligns the initial DetTid baseline for synchronous verification logging so it matches init_file_tracing. THAT MISMATCH IS ITSELF DETERMINISM-RELEVANT, so this is a real cost rather than bookkeeping.**
- ⚠️ **THE DEFECT IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE GOAL. Burning a DetTid by spawning and joining a host thread has a side effect on signal and timer delivery in the KVM sandbox — the sandbox is killed by SIGALRM, signal 14, with no comparison returned. ptrace is unaffected throughout. A fix achieving the same alignment WITHOUT spawning a thread satisfies both sides.**
- ⚠️ **THERE IS NO TEST COVERAGE IN EITHER DIRECTION: equalize_tracing_thread_number has THREE CALL SITES AND ZERO TESTS. So the revert goes green with nothing guarding 2945's intent, and a future reapplication would have nothing to catch this recurrence either. ADD COVERAGE AS PART OF THIS, or the same three lines come back and break the same cell again.**
- **THIS IS ON THE DETERMINISM PATH IN TRACING INIT, so it should be made deliberately rather than as a drive-by. Not urgent; the cell is unblocked either way.**
- **Verify:** the DetTid baseline matches init_file_tracing without a host thread being spawned, c-programs/setitimer-determinism passes under both kvm and ptrace, and a test exists that would fail if the alignment regressed.
